features.name: harness-verify keeps every gate's output in a last-run log
features.description: Queue item since feat-068: a one-off tests-gate failure left no output to read. harness-verify.sh printed a failing gate's output only to the console, and --json printed none of it.
acceptance_criteria: each gate's raw output, with its label, the same OK/SKIP/FAIL verdict as the JSON report and its exit code, is written to harness-verify-last.log next to harness-verify-last.json, also under --json; a missing gate script gets a SKIP line
the next run replaces the log
an unwritable or disabled last-report path changes neither the exit code nor the console output
features.evidence: scripts/harness-verify.sh: run_gate computes one verdict (OK, SKIP when a passing gate prints SKIP, FAIL) used for the console, the report and the log; it appends '=== <label>: <verdict> (exit N) ===' and the gate's output to a temp log, copied to ${LAST_REPORT%.json}.log with the kept report (same || true guard). gitleaks runs with --redact, so the log holds no raw secret; the log is 0600. test_harness_verify.sh: 3 new cases, each failed first (the SKIP case after a fresh-context reviewer found the log said OK for a skipped gate), then 35 passed, 0 failed, also under /bin/bash 3.2. Security reviewer: no defects.

features.name: subagent governance, concurrency limits and structured evidence rubrics
features.description: Add a subagent concurrency limit (<= 3) and evidence-over-assertion to the engineering rules, without changing the two-subagent review rule for high-risk changes (owner, 2026-10-20); augment EVALUATOR_RUBRIC in outside_agent.py with concrete failure scenarios and file:line evidence.
acceptance_criteria: agents/engineering-rules.md specifies concurrency limit <= 3 and empirical evidence over assertions, and carries no 1:1 inner/outside ratio or model-tier rule
scripts/outside_agent.py EVALUATOR_RUBRIC requires concrete failure scenarios for REJECT/CONDITIONAL and exact file:line anchors
tests/test_outside_agent.py asserts the rubric text carries each clause; scripts/tests/test_engineering_rules_scope.sh asserts the rules text
features.evidence: Rules text: cap and evidence rule added; the 1:1 ratio and model-tier bullets dropped (contradicted the 2026-10-20 owner decision). test_engineering_rules_scope.sh failed first (14/1), then 15/0. test_apply_rubric_structure failed first on 'subagent concurrency caps (<= 3)' against main; text assertions only. pytest test_outside_agent 234 passed; mypy clean; worktree gates: 9 OK, types skipped (mypy run by hand), runtime drift fails only until install.sh. After the fast-forward to main: install.sh and install-agents-md.sh run, 11 gates passed in the pre-push hook, all four host files carry the cap and evidence rules.

features.name: cve-audit skill: read-only CVE assessment for AWS EKS workloads
features.description: Public cross-agent skill (assess, doctor, setup) with a stdlib-only collector producing deterministic per-layer CVE verdicts for EKS workloads; private config, redacted reports, fail-closed permission rules. Spec and plan: docs/superpowers/.
acceptance_criteria: skills/cve-audit routes /cve-audit-assess, -doctor, -setup; registered local and core; installed for the selected agents
Verdicts come from a hash-validated advisory table and normalized shards, identical for any shard order; the four verdicts follow the spec's combination order
Reads are fixed-argv, scrubbed-env, read-only; Kubernetes is read only after account, region and cluster match; no Secret reads; reports alias environments and carry no identifiers
Auto-approval only when collector, config and approved hash are provably outside the agent's writable roots; unknown keeps prompts; setup removes only what it installed
Collector copies live in runtime_files, so the runtime-drift gate covers them
features.evidence: Commits 35da366..2b49b31 (plan tasks 1-9, then review fixes). Each task test-first; mutation checks on every security rule. skills/cve-audit pytest 457 passed, mypy clean, run-tests --fast 111/0, harness gates pass; collector runs on /usr/bin/python3 3.9.6. Two fresh-context reviews plus a re-review found 12 confirmed defects, all fixed test-first. Known gaps (exposure/AMI not collected, six tested helpers unwired, Inspector shapes and Codex rule unverified against real services): docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-06-cve-audit-skill.md, Delivery status.

features.name: polish-input hands off to the runtime venv interpreter
features.description: A Homebrew bump of python3 (3.14 to 3.15) left the venv's compiled wheels (anthropic -> jiter) unloadable under the hook's bare python3, so every prompt logged no-change. polish.py now re-execs under ~/.<repo-id>/venv/bin/python once (POLISH_REEXEC guards a loop) and falls back to the current interpreter if that python is missing.
acceptance_criteria: With a runtime venv python present, the hook runs under it exactly once
POLISH_REEXEC set, or no usable venv python, leaves the hook on the current interpreter and still fails open
features.evidence: New tests failed first (no hand-off), then 63 passed. Live hook under python3 3.15.2 turned 'i want add new feature for login' into a polished line, where before it returned no-change. mypy clean. Not fixed: the engine-error hint is deduped by reason hash, so the Oct 22 marker hid this recurrence; deferred.
